videos.title: How U.S. Aircraft Carriers Operate During the Iran War  | WSJ Equipped
videos.description:
The aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt has arrived in the Middle East to help the U.S. fend off Iranian attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, enforce the blockade and give President Trump expanded options to strike Iran should he choose to do so. The warship joins USS George Washington and USS George H.W. Bush, marking the second time this year that the U.S. has had three carriers in the Middle East. 

The U.S. has kept at least two carriers in the region since the war started, and so far five of the Navy’s 11 aircraft carriers have deployed to support the war. Two of those carriers, USS Gerald R. Ford and USS Abraham Lincoln, have set modern-day records for their length of deployment and their time at sea without a port call. The deployment of USS George H.W. Bush, which is in the Arabian Sea, has also been extended.

WSJ journalists visited USS George Washington in the Arabian Sea in October to learn more about how these carriers are conducting operations, and how the war is testing the limits of the Navy’s carrier strike groups. The carrier normally operates in the Western Pacific but was pulled into the Middle East in August to relieve the Lincoln.

videos.title: Nvidia In Crisis: The Rise Of Jensen Huang’s Empire At The Center Of The AI Boom
videos.description:
Nvidia is facing the biggest crisis in its 33 year history, with founder Jensen Huang resigning as CEO Thursday after admitting to having an affair with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, and accusations of two more affairs with employees inside his company. Now CFO Colette Kress has taken the helm as Nvidia’s interim CEO.

The implications of Jensen Huang’s affair with Alice Huang run far deeper than infidelity because her ties to Nvidia customer Megaspeed put her in the middle of a sprawling effort to accumulate AI chips across Southeast Asia. And Megaspeed is under investigation for possibly diverting restricted Nvidia chips into the hands of Chinese companies.

The relationship between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang dates back to 2023, according to The New York Times. It was a “turbulent” time for Nvidia, Jensen Huang told CNBC during an interview at the time, as the company navigated the first in a series of strict export controls the Biden administration placed on sending its most advanced chips to China.

On that same day we interviewed Jensen Huang in 2023, we also interviewed Huang’s direct report Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, with whom Jensen Huang is accused of having an affair.

Three years later, the long-time Nvidia CEO and founder has resigned, and CNBC takes a look back at our interviews with Jensen Huang and other Nvidia executives to get a clear picture of where Nvidia stands today, and all it stands to lose.

Recorded onboard the Royal Navy aircraft carrier HMS Prince of Wales docked in Oslo, host Lucy Fisher is joined by FT UK chief political commentator Robert Shrimsley and defence correspondent Charles Clover.

Together, they assess Europe’s response to Moscow's grey-zone tactics and the strategic role of the Joint Expeditionary Force (JEF) - a grouping of northern European countries led by Britain including the Nordics, Baltics and the Netherlands. Is it a focused response to the threat of Russia in the north, or could it weaken the power of Nato? 

And we hear from the secretary of state for defence, Wes Streeting, who told the FT this week that the UK and Russia need new back channels to avoid “miscalculation”. Plus, how does Britain balance its ambitious defence spending commitments against tight domestic budgets and political pressure?

This week’s episode is supported by Equinor. Everything we discuss is editorially independent.

• Financing, guarantees, and risk mitigation to help mobilize capital

videos.title: The Truth About How Data Centers Use Water And Power To Keep Cool
videos.description:
U.S. voters passed 40 ballot measures putting limits on AI data centers this week, as huge 1GW AI data centers from OpenAI, Meta, SpaceXAI, Amazon, Google and more push up water and power bills and put a strain on local resources. One of the issues that continues to come up is water usage, which is needed to cool the GPUs inside data centers running AI workloads. Closed-loop liquid cooling keeps water use low inside many modern AI data centers, but external cooling is still needed to move heat outside of the buildings and that requires large amounts of power or water in hot climates. CNBC visited data centers and spoke to researchers to find out the truth about how data centers use water.
